account: France's Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) runs “Foncier innovant”. A deep-learning algorithm finds building and pool outlines in public IGN aerial images. An automated check compares them to land-tax files. A tax agent verifies every anomaly before the owner is contacted. DGFiP's October 2021 note says that Capgemini provided project-management and build assistance and that Google provided the cloud infrastructure and services for developing the artificial-intelligence models. The 2022 experiment in nine departments led to more than 20,000 pools being taxed for 2022, close to €10 million of extra revenue for the communes concerned (DGFiP, 2 June 2023). The sources date the result only by the 2022 tax year. After generalization in 2023, the first pass covered metropolitan France, excluding Paris and the overseas departments (DROM). It detected 150,000 untaxed taxable pools. In its report of 15 November 2023 the Cour des comptes put the project's cost at 25.9 million euros over three years. It restated that the 2022 experiment in nine departments identified 20,000 undeclared pools and brought in 10 million euros for the communes. The court wrote that the scheme mainly demonstrates the capacity of the DGFiP to detect undeclared buildings. The Sénat's April 2024 report puts the cost at €24 million and calls the detected pools “potentiellement taxables”. Industrialization began in June 2024.

ai_role.statement: Official sources describe the chain (AI detection, automated file check, human verification, owner contact) and attribute the taxed pools to it. No evaluation isolates the algorithm's contribution from the human verification and declaration campaign. The Assemblée nationale written answer of 14 December 2021 confirms DGFiP's use of AI on IGN imagery and that contractors do not access tax data.

fields.account: France's Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) runs “Foncier innovant”. A deep-learning algorithm finds building and pool outlines in public IGN aerial images. An automated check compares them to land-tax files. A tax agent verifies every anomaly before the owner is contacted. DGFiP's October 2021 note says that Capgemini provided project-management and build assistance and that Google provided the cloud infrastructure and services for developing the artificial-intelligence models. The 2022 experiment in nine departments led to more than 20,000 pools being taxed for 2022, close to €10 million of extra revenue for the communes concerned (DGFiP, 2 June 2023). The sources date the result only by the 2022 tax year. After generalization in 2023, the first pass covered metropolitan France, excluding Paris and the overseas departments (DROM). It detected 150,000 untaxed taxable pools. In its report of 15 November 2023 the Cour des comptes put the project's cost at 25.9 million euros over three years. It restated that the 2022 experiment in nine departments identified 20,000 undeclared pools and brought in 10 million euros for the communes. The court wrote that the scheme mainly demonstrates the capacity of the DGFiP to detect undeclared buildings. The Sénat's April 2024 report puts the cost at €24 million and calls the detected pools “potentiellement taxables”. Industrialization began in June 2024.
